+def dep_layer_step(core, batch, q, contexts):
+    """One decode step of a real 96-head (TP1) K3.1 DSA layer through the stock
+    KimiK3DSAAttention forward and through runtime.dep.DepAttention.run_wide (the
+    DEP step's attention: split-K / cuBLAS projection, PreparedDsa at 96 heads,
+    o_proj), each over its own copy of the same caches (written by the stock
+    writers), on the same metadata. Returns both outputs, both rows entering
+    o_proj, the top-k and what the FP32 reference needs."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from tests.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_specialized_decode_dsa import (  # noqa: E501
+        GAP,
+        LAYER_CORES,
+        LAYER_HIDDEN,
+        UNIT,
+        assert_index_nan_free,
+        common_metadata,
+        dsa_layer,
+        index_row,
+        layer_config,
+        owned_slots,
+        paged_rows,
+    )
+    from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+    from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.forward_context import create_forward_context, override_forward_context
+    from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.ops.dsa_indexer import (
+        indexer_k_norm_quant_insert,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.ops.dsa_indexer_mxfp4 import (
+        mxfp4_k_norm_quant_insert,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.specialized_decode.cutedsl.dsa.attn_fi import (
+        fi_kernels,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.specialized_decode.runtime.dep import (
+        DepAttention,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.indexer import (
+        DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder,
+    )
+    from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import get_block_table_width
+
+    cache_dtype, _, kernel = LAYER_CORES[core]
+    config = layer_config(core, q)
+    length = config.model_config.max_model_len
+    row = {"fp8": FP8_ROW, "nvfp4_ds_mla": NVFP4_ROW}[cache_dtype]
+    dev = torch.device("cuda", torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
+    bf = torch.bfloat16
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+        topk_buffer = torch.full((length, 2048), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+        attn = dsa_layer(config, topk_buffer, HEADS)
+        layer, indexer = attn.mla_attn.mla_attn, attn.dsa_indexer
+        spec = layer.get_kv_cache_spec(config)
+        builder = layer.attn_backend.get_builder_cls()(
+            spec, [layer.layer_name], config, dev
+        )
+        index_spec = indexer.k_cache.get_kv_cache_spec(config)
+        index_builder = DeepseekV32IndexerMetadataBuilder(
+            index_spec,
+            [indexer.k_cache.prefix],
+            config,
+            dev,
+            block_table_width=get_block_table_width(
+                index_spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(config, length), UNIT
+            ),
+        )
+        reqs = batch // q
+        gen = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(batch + q)
+        contexts = [contexts[r % len(contexts)] + 3 * r for r in range(reqs)]
+        mla, mla_table = paged_rows([c + q for c in contexts], UNIT, row, UNIT, gen)
+        index, index_table = paged_rows(
+            [c + q for c in contexts], UNIT, index_row(indexer), GAP, gen
+        )
+        old = [range(c) for c in contexts]
+        old_mla = owned_slots(mla_table, old)
+        old_index = owned_slots(index_table, old)
+        n = old_mla.numel()
+        unit = torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
+        kv_c = torch.randn(n, 512, device=dev, dtype=bf, generator=gen)
+        k_pe = torch.randn(n, 64, device=dev, dtype=bf, generator=gen)
+        ops.concat_and_cache_mla(kv_c, k_pe, mla, old_mla, cache_dtype, unit)
+        keys = torch.randn(n, 128, device=dev, dtype=bf, generator=gen)
+        scratch = torch.empty(n, 2048, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+        norm = torch.ones(128, dtype=bf, device=dev)
+        args = (norm, torch.zeros_like(norm), EPS, old_index, index, scratch, n)
+        insert = indexer_k_norm_quant_insert
+        if indexer.use_fp4_cache:
+            insert = mxfp4_k_norm_quant_insert
+        insert(keys, *args)
+        assert_index_nan_free(index)
+        new = [range(c, c + q) for c in contexts]
+        new_mla = owned_slots(mla_table, new)
+        new_index = owned_slots(index_table, new)
+        hidden = torch.randn(batch, LAYER_HIDDEN, device=dev, dtype=bf, generator=gen)
+        positions = torch.tensor([p for pos in new for p in pos], device=dev)
+        names = layer.layer_name, indexer.k_cache.prefix
+
+        def step(mla_cache, index_cache):
+            layer.kv_cache, indexer.k_cache.kv_cache = mla_cache, index_cache
+            md = builder.build(0, common_metadata(contexts, q, mla_table, new_mla))
+            index_md = index_builder.build(
+                0, common_metadata(contexts, q, index_table, new_index)
+            )
+            context = create_forward_context(
+                dict(zip(names, (md, index_md))),
+                config,
+                slot_mapping=dict(zip(names, (new_mla, index_md.slot_mapping))),
+            )
+            return md, override_forward_context(context)
+
+        entering = []
+        hook = attn.o_proj.register_forward_pre_hook(
+            lambda _, args: entering.append(args[0].clone())
+        )
+        stock_mla, stock_index = mla.clone(), index.clone()
+        _, context = step(stock_mla, stock_index)
+        with context:
+            stock = attn(positions, hidden)
+        hook.remove()
+        stock_topk = topk_buffer[:batch].clone()
+
+        policy = dict(kernels=(kernel,)) if kernel not in (None, "auto") else {}
+        runtime = SimpleNamespace(
+            device=dev,
+            buffers={},
+            wide=(batch,),
+            queries=(q,),
+            fi_kernels=policy.get("kernels", fi_kernels(cache_dtype)),
+            prims_ts_rows=_prims_ts_row_buckets(config),
+        )
+        dep = DepAttention(SimpleNamespace(self_attn=attn), runtime)
+        ours_mla, ours_index = mla.clone(), index.clone()
+        md, context = step(ours_mla, ours_index)
+        dep.prepare_layout([ours_mla])
+        if dep.core.fused is not None:
+            dep.core.fused.write_ids(topk_buffer)
+        topk_buffer.fill_(-1)
+        with context:
+            out = dep.run_wide(hidden, [ours_mla], md, {names[0]: new_mla}, q)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        attn=attn,
+        out=out,
+        stock=stock,
+        local=dep.local[:batch].clone(),
+        entering=entering[0],
+        topk=topk_buffer[:batch].clone(),
+        stock_topk=stock_topk,
+        projected=dep.projected[:batch].clone(),
+        caches=(ours_mla, stock_mla),
+        mla_table=mla_table,
+        kv=cache_dtype,
+    )
+
+
 def relative(x, ref):
     return float((x.float() - ref.float()).norm() / ref.float().norm())
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("core", ["fi-auto", "fi-prims_ts"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("batch,q", [(5, 5), (20, 5), (80, 5), (8, 1)])
+def test_dep_attention_matches_stock_short_context(
+    workspace_init, dist_init, core, batch, q
+):
+    """DepAttention.run_wide against the stock 96-head DSA layer at contexts below
+    the top-k (2048): both attend over every token (no top-k tie can separate
+    them), and both pre-o_proj rows against FP32 attention over the dequantized
+    cache: ours at least as accurate as stock.
+
+    The two paths differ by ~2.8% (rel. RMS) at equal accuracy (~3.4% each vs
+    FP32), from two sources, both rounding-order effects (bisected stage by stage):
+    (1) the stock q_a / kv_a RMSNorm (native) rounds x * rstd to BF16 before the
+    weight multiply, ours rounds x * rstd * w once (the vllm_c kernel's math): 27%
+    of the q_c elements differ by one BF16 ulp, which flips ~10% of the FP8 query
+    codes (ours matches a single-rounding reference to <0.05% of bytes); (2) the FP8
+    sparse MLA kernels quantize P to E4M3 per KV tile, so the same top-k set in another
+    order changes the output by ~2.4% (the stock kernel against itself with its
+    top-k rows permuted); the fused indexer emits key order, stock's top-k its own
+    order. With identical inputs the core is the stock kernel."""
+    from tests.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_specialized_decode_dsa import (  # noqa: E501
+        layer_reference,
+    )
+
+    step = dep_layer_step(core, batch, q, (600, 1100, 1500, 1980, 37))
+    # Every token selected on both paths (contexts + q <= 2048).
+    for t in range(batch):
+        a = set(step.topk[t].tolist()) - {-1}
+        b = set(step.stock_topk[t].tolist()) - {-1}
+        assert a == b, t
+    # Each pre-o_proj row set against its own FP32 reference (same top-k).
+    args = step.attn, step.projected
+    ours_ref = layer_reference(
+        *args, step.caches[0], step.mla_table, step.topk, q, step.kv
+    )
+    stock_ref = layer_reference(
+        *args, step.caches[1], step.mla_table, step.stock_topk, q, step.kv
+    )
+    ours_err, stock_err = (
+        relative(step.local, ours_ref),
+        relative(step.entering, stock_ref),
+    )
+    between = relative(step.local, step.entering)
+    print(
+        f"pre-o_proj vs FP32: ours {ours_err:.4f} stock {stock_err:.4f}; "
+        f"ours vs stock {between:.4f}; layer output vs stock "
+        f"{relative(step.out, step.stock):.4f}"
+    )
+    assert ours_err <= 1.1 * stock_err + 1e-3, (ours_err, stock_err)
+    assert between < 0.04, between
+    assert relative(step.out, step.stock) < 0.04
+

+def dcp_merge_vs_exact(world, saturate, repeats=1):
+    """The specialized DCP decode's top-k merge (#63's dcp_topk_merge_rows, as
+    IndexerStage.merge_rows calls it on DeepGEMM-layout logits) against the exact
+    global top-2048 of the same scores. Every rank draws the same global scores
+    (distinct up to BF16 ties) of 32K-token rows and holds its interleave-1
+    shard; `saturate`: rank 0's keys score above every other rank's, so it
+    holds all 2048 of the global top-k (more than its N local candidates).
+    Compares the multiset of the merged ids' scores with the exact top-2048's
+    (exact selection up to ties), and each rank's rows with its owned ids.
+    `repeats`: merges the same scores that many times; every rank's rows must
+    come out bit-identical, order included (the sparse decode sums in it)."""
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+
+    from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed import get_dcp_group
+    from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.ops import dcp_topk_merge as merge_pkg
+    from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.ops.dcp_topk_merge.kernels import (
+        dcp_topk_merge_rows,
+    )
+
+    topk, local_len, rows, block = 2048, 4096, 6, UNIT
+    rank = get_dcp_group().rank_in_group
+    dev = torch.device("cuda", torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
+    config = layer_config("fi-trtllm", 1, world)
+    n = merge_pkg.dcp_merge_local_topk(topk, world)
+    assert n == 384, n  # DCP8: 1.5x the fair share, warp-aligned
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config):  # the rescue workspace (collective)
+        assert merge_pkg.init_dcp_topk_merge(config, topk) == n
+    assert merge_pkg.dcp_topk_merge_fits(rows, topk, n)
+    gen = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(29)
+    scores = torch.rand(rows, local_len * world, device=dev, generator=gen)
+    if saturate:
+        scores[:, 0::world] += 2  # rank 0 owns gid % world == 0
+    scores = scores.bfloat16()
+    # This rank's logits in DeepGEMM's layout (1 KiB-aligned BF16 rows).
+    logits = scores[:, rank::world].contiguous()
+    assert logits.stride(0) * 2 % 1024 == 0
+    row_ends = torch.full((rows,), local_len, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    req_id = torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    pages = local_len // block
+    table = torch.arange(rows * pages, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    table = table.view(rows, pages)
+    rows_out = torch.full((rows, topk), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    valid_out = torch.full((rows,), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    ids_out = torch.full((rows, topk), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    runs = []
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        rows_out.fill_(-7)
+        valid_out.fill_(-7)
+        dcp_topk_merge_rows(
+            logits=logits,
+            row_ends=row_ends,
+            max_local_len=local_len,
+            local_topk=n,
+            topk=topk,
+            req_id=req_id,
+            block_table=table,
+            block_size=block,
+            stride_rows=block,
+            dcp_rank=rank,
+            rows_out=rows_out,
+            valid_out=valid_out,
+            ids_out=ids_out,
+        )
+        runs.append((rows_out.clone(), valid_out.clone()))
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    for again, count in runs[1:]:
+        assert torch.equal(count, runs[0][1])
+        assert torch.equal(again, runs[0][0]), "the merged rows' order changed"
+    exact = torch.topk(scores.float(), topk, dim=1)
+    held = int((exact.indices[0] % world == 0).sum())
+    assert (held > n) == saturate, held  # the construction is (not) saturated
+    for t in range(rows):
+        ids = ids_out[t].long()
+        assert bool((ids >= 0).all()) and ids.unique().numel() == topk, t
+        got = scores[t, ids].float().sort(descending=True).values
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got, exact.values[t], atol=0, rtol=0)
+        mine = ids[ids % world == rank] // world  # this rank's local positions
+        assert int(valid_out[t]) == mine.numel(), t
+        want = (table[t, mine // block].long() * block + mine % block).sort().values
+        assert torch.equal(rows_out[t, : mine.numel()].long().sort().values, want), t
+    dist.barrier(get_dcp_group().cpu_group)
+

+"""FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE on FlashInfer's prims_ts sparse MLA kernel (SM100).
+
+Kimi K3.1 DSA shapes: D576, top-k capacity 2048, 96 query heads (DCP8 gathered
+heads; zero-padded to 128 for the 2-CTA schedule on FlashInfer builds that do
+not schedule 96 heads natively), per-tensor fp8 and
+nvfp4_ds_mla caches written by the production cache writer into a packed
+(BLHNC-strided) block layout. Every cache row no live index addresses (page 0,
+the other layers' rows between blocks, unselected rows, rows named by entries
+past a row's length) is NaN, so any stray read fails the comparison.
+"""
+
+import math
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.flashinfer import has_flashinfer_prims_ts_sparse_mla
+
+if not (
+    current_platform.is_cuda()
+    and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+    and has_flashinfer_prims_ts_sparse_mla()
+):

+        "needs SM100/SM103 and FlashInfer's prims_ts sparse MLA",
+        allow_module_level=True,
+    )
+

+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.sparse_utils import (  # noqa: E402
+    triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index,
+)
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops.dcp import CPTritonContext, correct_attn_out  # noqa: E402
+
+E4M3 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+KV_LORA_RANK, ROPE = 512, 64
+TOPK = 2048
+BLOCK_SIZE = 64
+# Packed layout: other layers' pages sit between this layer's blocks.
+BLOCK_STRIDE_ROWS = 3 * BLOCK_SIZE
+ROW_BYTES = {"fp8": 576, "nvfp4_ds_mla": 352}
+SCALE = 192**-0.5
+# Row capacities as _prims_ts_row_buckets plans them: powers of two (the test
+# shapes below have no CUDA graph sizes among them, so each row count below the
+# largest capacity runs on a larger plan with packed-query offsets).
+BUCKETS = tuple(1 << i for i in range(10))
+_E2M1 = [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0]
+
+
+def _impl(kv_cache_dtype: str, return_lse: bool = True, buckets=BUCKETS):
+    impl = object.__new__(fims.FlashInferMLASparseImpl)
+    impl.scale = SCALE
+    impl.kv_lora_rank = KV_LORA_RANK
+    impl.qk_rope_head_dim = ROPE
+    impl.use_prims_ts = True
+    impl.prims_ts_format = fims._PRIMS_TS_FORMATS[kv_cache_dtype]
+    impl.need_to_return_lse_for_decode = return_lse
+    impl.prims_ts_buckets = buckets
+    return impl
+
+
+def _cache(kv_cache_dtype: str, num_blocks: int, device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[num_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE, row bytes] uint8 view of a NaN-filled packed
+    buffer whose blocks are BLOCK_STRIDE_ROWS rows apart."""
+    raw = torch.full(
+        (num_blocks, BLOCK_STRIDE_ROWS, ROW_BYTES[kv_cache_dtype]),
+        0xFF,
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    return raw[:, :BLOCK_SIZE]
+
+
+def _write(cache, kv_cache_dtype, kv_c, k_pe, slots, k_scale):
+    """Production writer: token i into block slots[i] // BLOCK_SIZE, offset
+    slots[i] % BLOCK_SIZE."""
+    ops.concat_and_cache_mla(
+        kv_c,
+        k_pe,
+        cache,
+        slots.long(),
+        kv_cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype,
+        scale=torch.tensor(k_scale, dtype=torch.float32, device=kv_c.device),
+    )
+
+
+def _dequant_rows(cache, kv_cache_dtype, k_scale) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """fp32 [rows, 576] of every storage row (flat, packed stride), as the
+    kernel loads them: per-tensor e4m3 times the descale, or NVFP4 NoPE
+    expanded to e4m3(e2m1 * sf) (FlashInfer's loader) and unscaled e4m3 RoPE."""
+    rows, _ = fims.flat_kv_row_view(cache, BLOCK_SIZE)
+    if kv_cache_dtype == "fp8":
+        return rows.view(E4M3).float() * k_scale
+    table = torch.tensor(
+        _E2M1 + [-v for v in _E2M1], dtype=torch.float32, device=rows.device
+    )
+    packed = rows[:, :256]
+    nibbles = torch.stack([packed & 0xF, packed >> 4], -1).flatten(-2).long()
+    sf = rows[:, 320:352].unflatten(-1, (4, 8)).transpose(-1, -2).flatten(-2)
+    sf = sf.contiguous().view(E4M3).float()
+    nope = (table[nibbles].unflatten(-1, (32, 16)) * sf[..., None]).flatten(-2)
+    nope = nope.to(E4M3).float()
+    rope = rows[:, 256:320].contiguous().view(E4M3).float()
+    return torch.cat([nope, rope], -1)
+
+
+def _quant_q(q: torch.Tensor, q_scale: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The layer's static per-tensor E4M3 query quantization."""
+    t, h, d = q.shape
+    q8, _ = ops.scaled_fp8_quant(
+        q.reshape(t, h * d),
+        torch.tensor([q_scale], dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device),
+    )
+    return q8.view(t, h, d)
+
+
+def _reference(q8, q_scale, kv, indices, lengths):
+    """fp32 sparse attention; natural-log LSE; empty rows -> (0, -inf)."""
+    t, h, _ = q8.shape
+    out = torch.zeros(t, h, KV_LORA_RANK, device=q8.device)
+    lse = torch.full((t, h), -math.inf, device=q8.device)
+    q = q8.float() * q_scale
+    for i in range(t):
+        sel = indices[i, : lengths[i]]
+        sel = sel[sel >= 0].long()
+        if sel.numel() == 0:
+            continue
+        k = kv[sel]
+        s = q[i] @ k.T * SCALE
+        lse[i] = torch.logsumexp(s, -1)
+        out[i] = torch.softmax(s, -1) @ k[:, :KV_LORA_RANK]
+    return out, lse
+
+
+def _check(out, lse, ref_out, ref_lse, kv_cache_dtype):
+    assert out.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and lse.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert torch.isfinite(out).all(), "NaN/inf output: a masked row was read"
+    empty = torch.isinf(ref_lse)
+    assert torch.equal(torch.isinf(lse), empty)
+    assert (lse[empty] < 0).all() and (out[empty.nonzero(as_tuple=True)] == 0).all()
+    live = ~empty
+    if live.any():
+        o, r = out.float()[live], ref_out[live]
+        rel = ((o - r).norm() / r.norm()).item()
+        # E4M3 P (and the e4m3 Q/KV the reference already models).
+        assert rel < (2e-2 if kv_cache_dtype == "fp8" else 3e-2), rel
+        assert (lse[live] - ref_lse[live]).abs().max().item() < 2e-2
+
+
+def _problem(
+    kv_cache_dtype, counts, heads, k_scale, q_scale, seed, *, holes=False, blocks=None
+):
+    """Rows of local physical indices (compacted prefix, or with -1 holes
+    inside the prefix when `holes`) over live packed rows; entries past each
+    row's length name poisoned rows."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    dev = torch.device("cuda")
+    num_blocks = blocks or 1 + math.ceil(max(max(counts), 1) * 2 / BLOCK_SIZE) + 4
+    cache = _cache(kv_cache_dtype, num_blocks, dev)
+    # Live tokens: every slot of blocks 1.. (page 0 stays poisoned).
+    live_slots = torch.arange(BLOCK_SIZE, num_blocks * BLOCK_SIZE, device=dev)
+    phys = (live_slots // BLOCK_SIZE) * BLOCK_STRIDE_ROWS + live_slots % BLOCK_SIZE
+    t = len(counts)
+    indices = torch.empty((t, TOPK), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    lengths = torch.tensor(counts, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    used = torch.zeros(phys.numel(), dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)
+    for i, c in enumerate(counts):
+        perm = torch.randperm(phys.numel(), generator=g, device=dev)
+        row = phys[perm[:c]].to(torch.int32)
+        if holes and c > 2:
+            row[torch.randperm(c, generator=g, device=dev)[: c // 4]] = -1
+        used[perm[:c]] |= row >= 0
+        # Past the length: poisoned rows (page 0 and inter-block rows).
+        tail = torch.randint(0, BLOCK_STRIDE_ROWS, (TOPK - c,), generator=g, device=dev)
+        tail = torch.where(tail < BLOCK_SIZE, tail, tail % 7 + BLOCK_SIZE)
+        indices[i] = torch.cat([row, tail.to(torch.int32)])
+    # Write only the selected tokens; every other row stays NaN.
+    kv_c = torch.randn(phys.numel(), KV_LORA_RANK, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.2
+    k_pe = torch.randn(phys.numel(), ROPE, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.5
+    sel = used.nonzero().squeeze(1)
+    _write(
+        cache,
+        kv_cache_dtype,
+        kv_c[sel].bfloat16(),
+        k_pe[sel].bfloat16(),
+        live_slots[sel],
+        k_scale,
+    )
+    q = torch.randn(t, heads, KV_LORA_RANK + ROPE, generator=g, device=dev)
+    q8 = _quant_q(q.bfloat16() * 4, q_scale)
+    return cache, q8, indices, lengths
+
+
+COUNTS = {
+    # DCP8 local: about 1/8 of 2048, not multiples of 128, some empty.
+    "dcp_local": [0, 1, 37, 128, 129, 251, 256, 300, 0, 255, 383, 512],
+    "decode_b1": [251],
+    "full": [2048, 2047, 1, 0, 1000],
+}

+        q_len

+    k_pe = torch.randn(sum(seq_lens), ROPE, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.5

+    )

+    impl = _impl(kv_cache_dtype)

+def _f_pad_query_heads(query, heads):
+    """The zero head pad as the trtllm-gen call did it before (`F.pad`)."""
+    return torch.nn.functional.pad(query, (0, 0, 0, heads - query.shape[1]))

+def _masked_fill_dcp_partials(topk):
+    """trtllm-gen's empty-row guard before: an `all(topk == -1)` reduction,
+    then full `masked_fill`s of the output and LSE views."""
+
+    def finish(out, lse, counts):
+        empty = (topk == -1).all(dim=-1)
+        out.masked_fill_(empty.view(-1, 1, 1), 0.0)
+        lse.masked_fill_(empty.view(-1, 1), float("-inf"))
+
+    return finish
+

+    the reduction and masked fills did: output 0 and LSE -inf for rows whose
+    entries are all -1 (count 0; the kernel leaves garbage there), the other
+    rows untouched, and nothing outside the call's heads, including the next
+    row of an unpadded buffer when the row is not a whole number of the
+    kernel's output blocks (12 heads)."""

+    counts[::5] = 0
+    counts = counts.int()
+    slots = torch.arange(TOPK, device="cuda")
+    topk = torch.randint(0, 1 << 20, (tokens, TOPK), generator=g, device="cuda")
+    topk = topk.int().masked_fill(slots >= counts[:, None], -1)
+    out = torch.randn(tokens, buffer_heads, KV_LORA_RANK, generator=g, device="cuda")
+    out = out.bfloat16()
+    lse = torch.randn(tokens, buffer_heads, generator=g, device="cuda") * 30
+    out[counts == 0] = float("nan")
+    lse[counts == 0] = float("nan")
+    ref_out, ref_lse = out.clone(), lse.clone()
+    fims._finish_dcp_partials(out[:, :heads], lse[:, :heads], counts)
+    _masked_fill_dcp_partials(topk)(ref_out[:, :heads], ref_lse[:, :heads], counts)

@@ -0,0 +1,579 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tune or benchmark BatchedTritonExperts, the Triton kernel behind the
+batched expert-parallel MoE activation format (E x capacity x K).
+
+``benchmark_moe.py`` only ever instantiates ``TritonOrDeepGemmExperts``, so
+this is the tuning entry point for the batched kernel. It reuses the same
+mechanisms: ``override_config()`` forces a candidate through the real code
+path, and results use the ``E=...,N=...,device_name=...json`` naming so they
+drop straight into ``vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/`` or
+``VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER``.
+
+What differs from ``benchmark_moe.py``:
+
+* The lookup key is the per-expert *capacity*, ``hidden_states.size(1)`` of the
+  ``[E_local, capacity, K]`` tensor, not a token count. With the
+  ``alltoall_batched`` dispatch it is ``max_num_batched_tokens * ep_size``.
+* ``E`` is the number of *local* experts (``E_global / ep_size``) and ``N`` is
+  the full ``moe_intermediate_size``: with expert parallelism the MoE layers are
+  not tensor-parallel.
+* Only some keys reach the kernel: ``BLOCK_SIZE_M/N/K`` everywhere, plus
+  ``num_warps``, ``num_stages`` and ``grf_mode`` on XPU.
+* The batch is routed over ``E_global = E_local * ep_size`` experts and only the
+  rows landing on local experts are kept, so each local expert holds roughly
+  ``tokens * topk / E_global`` rows, as in a real EP run. Each candidate is
+  timed at several fill levels (share of the capacity that is populated), and
+  ranked by the geometric mean, so a config that wins on full prefill batches
+  does not lose on decode-sized ones.
+* Every candidate is checked against ``torch_experts`` before it may win.
+
+Examples (run from the vllm repo root)::
+
+    # Tune Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, K=2048, N=768, topk=8) for EP=4
+    python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_batched_moe.py tune \\
+        --num-experts 32 --ep-size 4 --hidden-size 2048 \\
+        --intermediate-size 768 --topk 8 \\
+        --capacity 1024 2048 4096 --save-dir ./tuned
+
+    # Latency of whatever the lookup resolves to (built-in heuristic, or the
+    # configs in VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER), with a correctness check
+    VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER=./tuned/merged \\
+    python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_batched_moe.py bench \\
+        --num-experts 32 --ep-size 4 --hidden-size 2048 \\
+        --intermediate-size 768 --topk 8 --capacity 1024 2048 4096
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import gc
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import statistics
+import time
+from datetime import datetime
+from itertools import product
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from tests.kernels.utils import torch_experts
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import fused_moe as fused_moe_module
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import fused_topk, override_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (
+    FusedMoEConfig,
+    FusedMoEParallelConfig,
+    FusedMoEQuantConfig,
+    RoutingMethodType,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.experts.fused_batched_moe import (
+    BatchedTritonExperts,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe import get_config_file_name
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.modular_kernel import FusedMoEKernel
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.batched import (
+    BatchedPrepareAndFinalize,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import triton
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager
+
+DEVICE = current_platform.device_type
+VLLM_CONFIG = VllmConfig()
+
+# Share of the capacity that is populated with tokens. 1.0 is a full batch;
+# the small values mimic decode steps, where most of the slots stay empty.
+DEFAULT_FILLS = (1.0, 0.1, 0.01)
+
+
+def get_search_space() -> list[dict[str, int | str]]:
+    """Only parameters the batched kernel actually consumes."""
+    if current_platform.is_xpu():
+        # Mirrors benchmark_moe.get_xpu_tuning_space. GROUP_SIZE_M is left out:
+        # the batched kernel has no such parameter.
+        param_ranges: dict[str, list[int] | list[str]] = {
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_M": [16, 32, 64, 128, 256],
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_N": [64, 128],
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_K": [32, 64],
+            "num_warps": [4, 8, 16],
+            "num_stages": [3, 4],
+            "grf_mode": ["128", "256"],
+        }
+    else:
+        # num_warps/num_stages are not read by the kernel on CUDA.
+        param_ranges = {
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_M": [16, 32, 64, 128, 256],
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_N": [32, 64, 128, 256],
+            "BLOCK_SIZE_K": [64, 128, 256],
+        }
+    keys, values = zip(*param_ranges.items())
+    return [dict(zip(keys, combo)) for combo in product(*values)]
+
+
+def sync() -> None:
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+
+def clear_triton_cache() -> None:
+    gc.collect()
+    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+    try:
+        if hasattr(triton.runtime, "cache") and hasattr(triton.runtime.cache, "clear"):
+            triton.runtime.cache.clear()
+    except Exception as e:  # best effort only
+        print(f"warning: failed to clear Triton cache: {e}")
+    gc.collect()
+
+
+def make_dummy_moe_config(max_num_tokens: int) -> FusedMoEConfig:
+    """Most fields are unused by the config lookup; the constructor of the
+    modular kernel just needs the object (see tests/kernels/moe/utils.py)."""
+    return FusedMoEConfig(
+        num_experts=1,
+        experts_per_token=1,
+        hidden_dim=1,
+        intermediate_size=1,
+        num_local_experts=1,
+        num_logical_experts=1,
+        moe_parallel_config=FusedMoEParallelConfig.make_no_parallel(),
+        activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
+        in_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device=DEVICE,
+        routing_method=RoutingMethodType.TopK,
+        max_num_tokens=max_num_tokens,
+    )
+
+
+def build_kernel(capacity: int, num_local_experts: int) -> FusedMoEKernel:
+    quant_config = FusedMoEQuantConfig.make(
+        None, per_act_token_quant=False, block_shape=None
+    )
+    return FusedMoEKernel(
+        BatchedPrepareAndFinalize(
+            capacity,
+            num_dispatchers=1,
+            num_local_experts=num_local_experts,
+            rank=0,
+        ),
+        BatchedTritonExperts(
+            max_num_tokens=capacity,
+            num_dispatchers=1,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            moe_config=make_dummy_moe_config(capacity),
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+class Problem:
+    """Weights plus one routed batch per fill level for a given capacity.
+
+    ``BatchedPrepareAndFinalize`` sizes the expert tensor as
+    ``min(capacity, num_tokens)`` rows, and that size is the config lookup key.
+    To keep the key at ``capacity`` for every fill level, the batch always has
+    ``capacity`` tokens and the unused ones are routed to a non-existent expert
+    id, so they are dropped by the dispatch.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        capacity: int,
+        num_local_experts: int,
+        ep_size: int,
+        N: int,
+        K: int,
+        topk: int,
+        fills: tuple[float, ...],
+    ):
+        self.capacity = capacity
+        self.E = num_local_experts
+        E_global = num_local_experts * ep_size
+        self.fills = fills
+
+        self.a = torch.randn((capacity, K), device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+        # w1 is the fused gate+up projection [E, 2N, K]; w2 is [E, K, N].
+        self.w1 = (
+            torch.randn(
+                (num_local_experts, 2 * N, K), device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+            )
+            / 15
+        )
+        self.w2 = (
+            torch.randn((num_local_experts, K, N), device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            / 15
+        )
+
+        score = torch.randn((capacity, E_global), device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        topk_weight, topk_ids, _ = fused_topk(self.a, score, topk, False)
+
+        self.batches = []
+        for fill in fills:
+            num_active = max(1, int(round(capacity * fill)))
+            active = torch.arange(capacity, device=DEVICE) < num_active
+            ids = torch.where(active[:, None], topk_ids, E_global)
+            local = ids < num_local_experts
+            self.batches.append(
+                {
+                    "fill": fill,
+                    "weight": topk_weight,
+                    "ids": ids,
+                    "has_local": local.any(dim=1),
+                    "reference": torch_experts(
+                        self.a,
+                        self.w1,
+                        self.w2,
+                        torch.where(local, topk_weight, 0),
+                        torch.where(local, ids, 0),
+                    ),
+                    "rows_per_expert": local.sum().item() / num_local_experts,
+                }
+            )
+
+
+def run_once(kernel: FusedMoEKernel, problem: Problem, batch: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return kernel.apply(
+        problem.a,
+        problem.w1,
+        problem.w2,
+        batch["weight"],
+        batch["ids"],
+        # Only the local experts exist on this rank; ids >= E_local are dropped
+        # by the dispatch. The activation step on CUDA checks this count.
+        global_num_experts=problem.E,
+        activation=MoEActivation.SILU,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+        expert_map=None,
+    )
+
+
+def time_us(fn, num_iters: int, num_warmup: int) -> float:
+    for _ in range(num_warmup):
+        fn()
+    sync()
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    for _ in range(num_iters):
+        fn()
+    sync()
+    return (time.perf_counter() - start) / num_iters * 1e6
+
+
+def measure(
+    kernel: FusedMoEKernel,
+    problem: Problem,
+    config: dict | None,
+    num_iters: int,
+    num_warmup: int,
+    atol: float,
+    rtol: float,
+) -> list[float]:
+    """Latency (us) per fill level, or raises if the config is invalid."""
+    latencies = []
+    for batch in problem.batches:
+
+        def run(batch=batch):
+            if config is None:
+                return run_once(kernel, problem, batch)
+            with override_config(config):

+    return math.exp(sum(math.log(v) for v in values) / len(values))
+

+def tune_one_capacity(args, capacity: int) -> dict | None:
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VLLM_CONFIG):

+        problem = Problem(
+            capacity,
+            args.num_experts,
+            args.ep_size,
+            args.intermediate_size,
+            args.hidden_size,
+            args.topk,
+            tuple(args.fills),
+        )
+        kernel = build_kernel(capacity, args.num_experts)

+        baseline = measure(
+            kernel, problem, None, args.num_iters, args.num_warmup, args.atol, args.rtol
+        )
+
+        best: dict | None = None
+        # With --max-regression: the best candidate that is at most that much
+        # slower than the default at every fill, else the least-regressing one.
+        best_ok: dict | None = None
+        least_bad: dict | None = None
+        search_space = get_search_space()
+        for idx, config in enumerate(search_space):
+            try:
+                latencies = measure(
+                    kernel,
+                    problem,
+                    config,
+                    args.num_iters,
+                    args.num_warmup,
+                    args.atol,
+                    args.rtol,
+                )
+            except triton.runtime.autotuner.OutOfResources:
+                continue
+            except AssertionError as e:
+                print(f"  capacity={capacity} config#{idx} failed correctness: {e}")
+                continue
+            except Exception as e:
+                print(
+                    f"  capacity={capacity} config#{idx} raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
+                )
+                continue

+            score = geomean(latencies)
+            candidate = {"config": config, "score_us": score, "latencies_us": latencies}
+            if best is None or score < best["score_us"]:
+                best = candidate
+            if args.max_regression is not None:
+                worst = max(t / b for t, b in zip(latencies, baseline))
+                candidate["worst_ratio"] = worst
+                if worst <= 1 + args.max_regression and (
+                    best_ok is None or score < best_ok["score_us"]
+                ):
+                    best_ok = candidate
+                if least_bad is None or worst < least_bad["worst_ratio"]:
+                    least_bad = candidate
+
+            if (
+                args.cache_clear_interval > 0
+                and idx
+                and idx % args.cache_clear_interval == 0
+            ):
+                clear_triton_cache()
+        clear_triton_cache()
+
+    if best is None:
+        return None
+    if args.max_regression is not None:
+        best = best_ok or least_bad
+        best["constraint_met"] = best_ok is not None
+    best["baseline_us"] = baseline
+    best["rows_per_expert"] = [b["rows_per_expert"] for b in problem.batches]
+    return best

+def save_result(
+    save_dir: str, E: int, N: int, capacity: int, result: dict, args

+    filename = get_config_file_name(E, N, dtype=None, block_shape=None)
+    out_dir = os.path.join(save_dir, f"capacity_{capacity}")
+    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
+    path = os.path.join(out_dir, filename)
+    payload = {"triton_version": triton.__version__, str(capacity): result["config"]}
+    with open(path + ".tmp", "w") as f:
+        json.dump(payload, f, indent=4)
+        f.write("\n")

+        "device": current_platform.get_device_name(),
+        "triton_version": triton.__version__,
+        "E_local": E,
+        "ep_size": args.ep_size,
+        "N": N,
+        "K": args.hidden_size,
+        "topk": args.topk,
+        "capacity": capacity,
+        "fills": args.fills,
+        "rows_per_expert": result["rows_per_expert"],
+        "tuned_us": result["latencies_us"],
+        "baseline_us": result["baseline_us"],
+        "config": result["config"],
+        "constraint_met": result.get("constraint_met"),
+    }
+    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, filename + ".report.json"), "w") as f:
+        json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
+        f.write("\n")
+    return path
+
+
+def cmd_tune(args) -> None:
+    for capacity in args.capacity:
+        t0 = datetime.now()
+        try:
+            result = tune_one_capacity(args, capacity)
+        except Exception as e:  # e.g. OOM at the largest capacities
+            print(f"capacity={capacity}: SKIPPED, {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
+            clear_triton_cache()
+            continue
+        elapsed = (datetime.now() - t0).total_seconds()
+        if result is None:
+            print(f"capacity={capacity}: NO VALID CONFIG FOUND ({elapsed:.0f}s)")
+            continue
+        path = save_result(
+            args.save_dir,
+            args.num_experts,
+            args.intermediate_size,
+            capacity,
+            result,
+            args,
+        )
+        pairs = ", ".join(
+            f"fill={f}: {t:.0f}us vs default {b:.0f}us ({(b - t) / b * 100:+.1f}%)"
+            for f, t, b in zip(
+                args.fills, result["latencies_us"], result["baseline_us"]
+            )
+        )
+        regress = any(
+            t > 1.05 * b for t, b in zip(result["latencies_us"], result["baseline_us"])
+        )
+        print(
+            f"capacity={capacity}: {pairs} -> {path} ({elapsed:.0f}s)"
+            + ("  [REGRESSION >5% at some fill]" if regress else "")
+            + (
+                "  [NO CONFIG MEETS --max-regression, kept the least-regressing]"
+                if result.get("constraint_met") is False

+        )
+
+
+def cmd_bench(args) -> None:
+    """Latency through the real config lookup (tuned files if present) next to the
+    built-in default, measured alternately in one process so that host/GPU drift
+    cancels out."""
+    out = {}

+            problem = Problem(
+                capacity,
+                args.num_experts,
+                args.ep_size,
+                args.intermediate_size,
+                args.hidden_size,
+                args.topk,
+                tuple(args.fills),
+            )
+            kernel = build_kernel(capacity, args.num_experts)
+            runs = (args.num_iters, args.num_warmup, args.atol, args.rtol)
+            tuned_rounds, default_rounds = [], []
+            for _ in range(args.rounds):
+                tuned_rounds.append(measure(kernel, problem, None, *runs))
+                with mock.patch.object(fused_moe_module, "get_moe_configs", _no_tuned):
+                    default_rounds.append(measure(kernel, problem, None, *runs))
+        tuned = [statistics.median(col) for col in zip(*tuned_rounds)]
+        default = [statistics.median(col) for col in zip(*default_rounds)]
+        out[capacity] = {
+            "fills": list(args.fills),
+            "tuned_us": tuned,
+            "default_us": default,
+        }
+        print(
+            f"capacity={capacity}: "
+            + ", ".join(
+                f"fill={f}: {t:.0f}us vs default {d:.0f}us ({(d - t) / d * 100:+.1f}%)"
+                for f, t, d in zip(args.fills, tuned, default)
+            )
+        )
+    if args.out_json:
+        with open(args.out_json, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(
+                {
+                    "device": current_platform.get_device_name(),
+                    "triton_version": triton.__version__,
+                    "tuned_config_folder": os.environ.get("VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER"),
+                    "rounds": args.rounds,
+                    "results": out,
+                },
+                f,
+                indent=2,
+            )
+            f.write("\n")
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="mode", required=True)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Merge per-capacity tuned config files from benchmark_batched_moe.py into
+one final config file, ready to drop into VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER.
+
+Adapted from xpu_kernel_autotune_tutorial.md section 8's fused-MoE merge
+script: same completeness guard (a missing capacity fails loudly here
+instead of silently falling back to a neighbor's config at lookup time,
+fused_moe.py:1447) and the same single-triton-version guard.
+
+Usage:
+    python3 benchmarks/kernels/merge_batched_moe_configs.py \\
+        --root ./tuned \\
+        --num-experts 32 --intermediate-size 768 \\
+        --expected 1024 2048 4096 --out ./tuned/merged
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import glob
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+if str(_REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT))
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe import (  # noqa: E402
+    get_config_file_name,
+)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--root", required=True, help="dir containing capacity_*/ subdirs"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--num-experts", "-E", type=int, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--intermediate-size", "-N", type=int, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--expected",
+        type=int,
+        nargs="+",
+        required=True,
+        help="every capacity that must be present",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    filename = get_config_file_name(
+        args.num_experts, args.intermediate_size, dtype=None, block_shape=None
+    )
+    paths = glob.glob(os.path.join(args.root, "**", filename), recursive=True)
+    if not paths:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"no config files matching {filename!r} found under {args.root}"
+        )
+
+    merged: dict[int, dict] = {}
+    versions: set[str] = set()
+    for path in paths:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            data = json.load(f)
+        versions.add(data.pop("triton_version"))
+        for key, config in data.items():
+            capacity = int(key)
+            if capacity in merged and merged[capacity] != config:
+                raise SystemExit(
+                    f"conflicting config for capacity {capacity} (see {path})"
+                )
+            merged[capacity] = config
+
+    missing = sorted(set(args.expected) - set(merged))
+    if missing:
+        raise SystemExit(f"missing capacities: {missing}")
+    if len(versions) != 1:
+        raise SystemExit(f"mixed Triton versions across inputs: {versions}")
+
+    result = {"triton_version": versions.pop()}
+    result.update({str(c): merged[c] for c in sorted(args.expected)})
+
+    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
+    destination = os.path.join(args.out, filename)
+    tmp = destination + ".tmp"
+    with open(tmp, "w") as f:
+        json.dump(result, f, indent=4)
+        f.write("\n")
+    os.replace(tmp, destination)
+    print(destination)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+import pytest
+import torch

+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.alltoall_batched import (

+)
+
+
+def make_pf(max_num_tokens: int, num_local_experts: int, num_dispatchers: int):
+    return AllToAllBatchedPrepareAndFinalize(
+        max_num_tokens=max_num_tokens,
+        num_local_experts=num_local_experts,
+        num_dispatchers=num_dispatchers,
+        rank=0,
+    )
+
+
+def worst_case_fill(topk_ids: torch.Tensor, num_local_experts: int, world: int):
+    """Replays prepare()'s packing, returning peak (token, slot, expert) usage."""
+    num_tokens, _ = topk_ids.shape
+    flat_expert = topk_ids.reshape(-1).to(torch.int64)
+    flat_token = torch.arange(num_tokens).repeat_interleave(topk_ids.size(1))
+    dest = torch.div(flat_expert, num_local_experts, rounding_mode="floor")
+
+    tok_fill, slot_fill = 0, 0
+    for r in range(world):
+        m = dest == r
+        toks, counts = torch.unique(flat_token[m], return_counts=True)
+        tok_fill = max(tok_fill, int(toks.numel()))
+        if counts.numel():
+            slot_fill = max(slot_fill, int(counts.max()))
+
+    local = flat_expert[dest == 0]
+    rows = torch.zeros(num_local_experts, dtype=torch.int64)
+    rows.index_add_(0, local, torch.ones(local.numel(), dtype=torch.int64))
+    # Every source rank may send an identical batch.
+    return tok_fill, slot_fill, int(rows.max()) * world
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "world,num_experts,topk",
+    [(2, 40, 8), (2, 40, 1), (4, 64, 6), (8, 256, 8), (8, 16, 8)],
+)
+def test_capacity_covers_random_routing(world, num_experts, topk):
+    max_num_tokens, e_local = 256, num_experts // world
+    pf = make_pf(max_num_tokens, e_local, world)
+    tok_cap, slots, expert_cap = pf.capacities(topk)
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    topk_ids = torch.stack(
+        [torch.randperm(num_experts)[:topk] for _ in range(max_num_tokens)]
+    )
+    tok_fill, slot_fill, expert_fill = worst_case_fill(topk_ids, e_local, world)
+
+    assert tok_fill <= tok_cap
+    assert slot_fill <= slots
+    assert expert_fill <= expert_cap
+
+
+def test_token_capacity_is_tight_when_all_tokens_target_one_rank():
+    """Dedup keeps the worst case token-sized rather than pair-sized."""
+    max_num_tokens, world, e_local, topk = 256, 2, 20, 8
+    pf = make_pf(max_num_tokens, e_local, world)
+    tok_cap, slots, _ = pf.capacities(topk)
+
+    topk_ids = torch.arange(topk).repeat(max_num_tokens, 1)
+    tok_fill, slot_fill, _ = worst_case_fill(topk_ids, e_local, world)
+
+    assert tok_fill == tok_cap
+    assert slot_fill == slots
+
+
+def test_expert_capacity_is_tight_when_all_tokens_pick_one_expert():
+    """One hot expert receives one row per token from every source rank."""
+    max_num_tokens, world, e_local = 256, 2, 20
+    pf = make_pf(max_num_tokens, e_local, world)
+    _, _, expert_cap = pf.capacities(topk=1)
+
+    topk_ids = torch.zeros((max_num_tokens, 1), dtype=torch.int64)
+    _, _, expert_fill = worst_case_fill(topk_ids, e_local, world)
+
+    assert expert_fill == expert_cap
+
+
+def test_activation_buffer_does_not_scale_with_topk():
+    """Only the int/float metadata may scale with topk, not the payload."""
+    pf = make_pf(max_num_tokens=256, num_local_experts=20, num_dispatchers=2)
+    tok_cap, slots, _ = pf.capacities(topk=8)
+    assert tok_cap == 256
+    assert slots == 8
+
+
+def test_slots_clamped_by_local_expert_count():
+    """A token cannot need more slots on a rank than that rank has experts."""
+    pf = make_pf(max_num_tokens=256, num_local_experts=2, num_dispatchers=8)
+    _, slots, _ = pf.capacities(topk=8)
+    assert slots == 2
+
+
+def test_expert_capacity_matches_batched_experts_workspace():
+    """b_a1's token dim must match BatchedTritonExperts.workspace_shapes()."""
+    pf = make_pf(max_num_tokens=256, num_local_experts=20, num_dispatchers=4)
+    _, _, expert_cap = pf.capacities(topk=8)
+    assert expert_cap == pf.max_num_tokens_per_rank() * pf.num_dispatchers()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import torch
+
+import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.modular_kernel as mk
+from vllm.distributed import get_ep_group
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import FusedMoEQuantConfig
+
+
+class AllToAllBatchedPrepareAndFinalize(mk.FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalizeModular):
+    """Routed all-to-all EP dispatch/combine in the batched activation format,
+    over fixed-capacity all_to_all_single collectives. A token is sent to a
+    destination rank once, however many of its experts live there, carrying
+    its local expert ids and router weights as metadata.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        max_num_tokens: int,
+        num_local_experts: int,
+        num_dispatchers: int,
+        rank: int,
+        is_sequence_parallel: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.max_num_tokens = max_num_tokens
+        self.num_local_experts = num_local_experts
+        self._num_dispatchers = num_dispatchers
+        self.rank = rank
+        self.is_sequence_parallel = is_sequence_parallel
+        self._combine_ctx: dict | None = None
+
+    @property
+    def activation_format(self) -> mk.FusedMoEActivationFormat:
+        return mk.FusedMoEActivationFormat.BatchedExperts
+
+    def max_num_tokens_per_rank(self) -> int | None:
+        return self.max_num_tokens
+
+    def topk_indices_dtype(self) -> torch.dtype | None:
+        return None
+
+    def num_dispatchers(self) -> int:
+        return self._num_dispatchers
+
+    def capacities(self, topk: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+        """Returns token slots per rank, expert slots per token, rows per expert."""
+        tok_cap = self.max_num_tokens
+        slots_per_token = min(topk, self.num_local_experts)
+        expert_cap = self.max_num_tokens * self._num_dispatchers
+        return tok_cap, slots_per_token, expert_cap
+
+    def output_is_reduced(self) -> bool:
+        return True
+
+    def prepare(
+        self,
+        a1: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        num_experts: int,
+        expert_map: torch.Tensor | None,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+        quant_config: FusedMoEQuantConfig,
+        defer_input_quant: bool = False,
+    ) -> mk.PrepareResultType:
+        if quant_config.quant_dtype is not None or defer_input_quant:
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                f"{self.__class__.__name__} supports unquantized MoE only."
+            )

+        h = a1.size(1)
+        num_tokens = a1.size(0)

+        dev = a1.device

+        if apply_router_weight_on_input:

+            )
+            a1 = a1 * topk_weights.to(a1.dtype)
+
+        flat_expert = topk_ids.reshape(-1).to(torch.int64)
+        flat_token = torch.arange(
+            num_tokens, device=dev, dtype=torch.int64
+        ).repeat_interleave(topk)
+        flat_weight = topk_weights.reshape(-1)
+        if apply_router_weight_on_input:
+            flat_weight = torch.ones_like(flat_weight)

+        # the dispatch, and their output rows stay zero.
+        routed = flat_expert >= 0

+        dest = torch.div(flat_expert, e_local, rounding_mode="floor")

+        # Deduplicate (dest, token) pairs so send_x stays token-sized.
+        order = torch.argsort(dest * (num_tokens + 1) + flat_token)
+        d_sorted, t_sorted = dest[order], flat_token[order]
+        new_slot = torch.ones_like(t_sorted, dtype=torch.bool)
+        new_slot[1:] = (d_sorted[1:] != d_sorted[:-1]) | (t_sorted[1:] != t_sorted[:-1])
+        slot_of_pair = new_slot.cumsum(0) - 1
+        uniq_dest = d_sorted[new_slot]
+        uniq_token = t_sorted[new_slot]
+        base = torch.zeros(world + 1, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+        # scatter_add_ instead of bincount: XPU's bincount rejects empty input.
+        per_dest = torch.zeros(world, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+        per_dest.scatter_add_(0, uniq_dest, torch.ones_like(uniq_dest))
+        base[1:] = per_dest.cumsum(0)
+        send_cnt = base[1:] - base[:-1]
+        local_slot = torch.arange(uniq_dest.numel(), device=dev) - base[uniq_dest]
+
+        send_x = torch.zeros((world, cap, h), dtype=a1.dtype, device=dev)
+        send_x[uniq_dest, local_slot] = a1.index_select(0, uniq_token)
+
+        # `pick` indexes a pair within its (dest, token) group, so the k-th
+        # expert a token wants on a rank lands in column k; -1 marks unused.
+        pair_ar = torch.arange(slot_of_pair.numel(), device=dev)
+        group_start = pair_ar[new_slot]
+        pair_slot = local_slot[slot_of_pair]
+        pick = pair_ar - group_start[slot_of_pair]
+        send_eloc = torch.full((world, cap, slots), -1, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+        send_eloc[d_sorted, pair_slot, pick] = flat_expert[order] - d_sorted * e_local
+
+        send_w = torch.zeros((world, cap, slots), dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
+        send_w[d_sorted, pair_slot, pick] = flat_weight[order].to(torch.float32)
+
+        # Fixed-size collectives, no host sync.
+        send_meta_pkt = torch.empty(
+            (world, cap * slots + 1), dtype=torch.int64, device=dev
+        )
+        send_meta_pkt[:, 0] = send_cnt
+        send_meta_pkt[:, 1:] = send_eloc.reshape(world, cap * slots)
+        recv_x = comm.all_to_all_single(send_x.reshape(world, cap * h)).reshape(
+            world, cap, h
+        )
+        recv_meta_pkt = comm.all_to_all_single(send_meta_pkt)
+        recv_w = comm.all_to_all_single(send_w.reshape(world, cap * slots)).reshape(
+            world, cap, slots
+        )
+        recv_cnt = recv_meta_pkt[:, 0].contiguous()
+        recv_eloc = recv_meta_pkt[:, 1:].reshape(world, cap, slots)
+
+        # Expand back to one row per (token, expert) pair.
+        slot_ar = torch.arange(cap, device=dev)
+        recv_valid = (slot_ar.view(1, -1) < recv_cnt.view(-1, 1)).unsqueeze(-1) & (
+            recv_eloc >= 0
+        )
+        vsrc, vslot, vpick = recv_valid.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
+        rows_x = recv_x[vsrc, vslot]
+        rows_e = recv_eloc[vsrc, vslot, vpick].clamp_(0, e_local - 1)

+

+        if n_recv > 0:
+            local_ids = torch.arange(e_local, device=dev).view(-1, 1)
+            hits = rows_e.view(1, -1) == local_ids
+            slots_all = hits.to(torch.int64).cumsum(dim=1) - 1
+            row_slot = slots_all[rows_e, torch.arange(n_recv, device=dev)]
+            keep = row_slot < expert_cap
+            b_a1[rows_e[keep], row_slot[keep]] = rows_x[keep]
+            tokens_per_expert[:e_local] = (
+                hits.sum(dim=1).clamp(max=expert_cap).to(torch.int32)
+            )
+        else:
+            row_slot = torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
+            keep = torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)
+
+        expert_tokens_meta = mk.ExpertTokensMetadata(
+            expert_num_tokens=tokens_per_expert, expert_num_tokens_cpu=None
+        )
+
+        self._combine_ctx = {
+            "world": world,
+            "cap": cap,
+            "h": h,
+            "dtype": a1.dtype,
+            "device": dev,
+            "num_tokens": num_tokens,
+            "vsrc": vsrc,
+            "vslot": vslot,
+            "rows_e": rows_e,
+            "rows_w": rows_w,
+            "row_slot": row_slot,
+            "keep": keep,
+            "n_recv": n_recv,
+            "send_cnt": send_cnt,
+            "uniq_dest": uniq_dest,
+            "uniq_token": uniq_token,

+        return b_a1, None, expert_tokens_meta, None, None

+    def finalize(
+        self,
+        output: torch.Tensor,
+        fused_expert_output: torch.Tensor,

+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+        weight_and_reduce_impl: mk.TopKWeightAndReduce,
+    ) -> None:
+        ctx = self._combine_ctx
+        assert ctx is not None, "finalize() called before prepare()"
+        comm = get_ep_group().device_communicator

+        send_out = comm.all_to_all_single(
+            recv_out.to(dtype).reshape(world, cap * h)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Finding amdgpu's exact VRAM counter from KFD topology and DRM sysfs. Plain
+files in a temporary directory, so this runs without a GPU."""
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.platforms.rocm_device_memory import find_vram_used_file
+
+GB = 1 << 30
+# torch's ROCm UUID holds the KFD unique_id 0x13a691b49a73a35c as ASCII hex.
+UUID = b"13a691b49a73a35c".hex()
+UNIQUE_ID = 0x13A691B49A73A35C
+# location_id 0xE300 is PCI bus 0xE3, device 0, function 0.
+PCI = (0, 0xE3, 0)
+
+
+def _node(root, name, **props):
+    node = root / "nodes" / name
+    node.mkdir(parents=True)
+    node.joinpath("properties").write_text(
+        "".join(f"{k} {v}\n" for k, v in props.items())
+    )
+
+
+def _gpu(root, name="2", minor=128, location_id=0xE300, unique_id=UNIQUE_ID):
+    _node(
+        root,
+        name,
+        simd_count=128,
+        drm_render_minor=minor,
+        location_id=location_id,
+        domain=0,
+        unique_id=unique_id,
+    )
+
+
+def _vram(root, minor=128, total=32 * GB, used=GB):
+    device = root / "drm" / f"renderD{minor}" / "device"
+    device.mkdir(parents=True)
+    device.joinpath("mem_info_vram_total").write_text(f"{total}\n")
+    device.joinpath("mem_info_vram_used").write_text(f"{used}\n")
+    return str(device / "mem_info_vram_used")
+
+
+def _find(root, uuid=UUID, pci=PCI, total=32 * GB):
+    return find_vram_used_file(
+        uuid,
+        pci,
+        total,
+        nodes_dir=str(root / "nodes"),
+        drm_dir=str(root / "drm"),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def root(tmp_path):
+    # A CPU node, skipped by the lookup.
+    _node(tmp_path, "0", simd_count=0, drm_render_minor=0, location_id=0)
+    return tmp_path
+
+
+def test_finds_the_gpu_by_uuid_and_pci(root):
+    _gpu(root)
+    _gpu(root, name="3", minor=129, location_id=0x6300, unique_id=7)
+    expected = _vram(root)
+    _vram(root, minor=129)
+    assert _find(root) == (expected, "")
+    # A UUID that is not hex digits leaves the PCI address.
+    assert _find(root, uuid="GPU-1234") == (expected, "")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("uuid", "pci"),
+    [
+        (UUID, (0, 0x99, 0)),  # no node at this PCI address
+        (b"0000000000000007".hex(), PCI),  # the node at this address has
+        # another unique_id
+    ],
+)
+def test_no_matching_node(root, uuid, pci):
+    _gpu(root)
+    _vram(root)
+    path, reason = _find(root, uuid=uuid, pci=pci)
+    assert path is None and "no single KFD node" in reason
+
+
+def test_skips_partitioned_gpus(root):
+    """Partitions of one GPU share its PCI bus and device (function 1 here)
+    and its VRAM counter."""
+    _gpu(root)
+    _gpu(root, name="3", minor=129, location_id=0xE301, unique_id=7)
+    _vram(root)
+    _vram(root, minor=129)
+    assert _find(root) == (None, "partitioned GPU")
+
+
+def test_skips_a_malformed_node(root):
+    """A node whose properties do not parse is skipped, not a crash."""
+    _gpu(root, unique_id="not-a-number")
+    _vram(root)
+    path, reason = _find(root)
+    assert path is None and "no single KFD node" in reason
+
+
+def test_needs_the_vram_counters(root):
+    _gpu(root)
+    path, reason = _find(root)
+    assert path is None and "no amdgpu VRAM counters" in reason
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("vram_total", "found"),
+    [
+        (32 * GB, True),
+        (int(32 * GB * 1.005), True),
+        # More than 1% above HIP's total: HIP's memory is not this VRAM.
+        (int(32 * GB * 1.02), False),
+        # Below HIP's total (e.g. an APU's small carve-out).
+        (32 * GB - (1 << 20), False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_vram_total_must_match_hip(root, vram_total, found):
+    _gpu(root)
+    expected = _vram(root, total=vram_total)
+    path, reason = _find(root)
+    assert path == (expected if found else None)
+    assert found or "does not match" in reason
+
+
+def test_no_kfd_topology(tmp_path):
+    path, reason = _find(tmp_path)
+    assert path is None and "no KFD topology" in reason

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Free memory by the exact device memory count on a real ROCm GPU. The sysfs
+lookup is tested without a GPU in tests/utils_/test_rocm_vram_lookup.py."""
+
+import ctypes
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    # vllm.platforms.rocm queries the GPU at import time.
+    pytest.skip("requires ROCm", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.platforms import rocm_device_memory  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.utils.extensible_tensor import ExtensibleTensor  # noqa: E402
+
+MB = 1 << 20
+DEVICE = torch.device("cuda:0")
+
+
+def _used() -> int:
+    path = rocm_device_memory._vram_used_file(0)
+    assert path is not None
+    with open(path) as f:
+        return int(f.read())
+
+
+def _exact_free() -> int:
+    free = rocm_device_memory.exact_free_memory(DEVICE)
+    assert free is not None
+    return free
+
+
+def _hidden() -> int:
+    """Free memory the exact count shows and HIP's free memory does not."""
+    return _exact_free() - torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(DEVICE)[0]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def exact_count():
+    torch.zeros(1, device=DEVICE)
+    if rocm_device_memory._vram_used_file(0) is None:
+        pytest.skip("no exact VRAM count for this GPU")
+    # Wait until earlier frees are erased and the count holds.
+    torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    start = held_since = time.monotonic()
+    last = _used()
+    while time.monotonic() - held_since < 0.1:
+        assert time.monotonic() - start < 10, "device memory never settled"
+        time.sleep(0.005)
+        if (used := _used()) != last:
+            held_since, last = time.monotonic(), used
+
+
+def test_exact_count_grows_with_an_allocation(exact_count):
+    before = _used()
+    tensor = torch.empty(64 * MB, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEVICE)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    grown = _used() - before
+    del tensor
+    # 64 MB, give or take driver memory (page tables).
+    assert abs(grown - 64 * MB) < 32 * MB
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def code_objects():
+    """Loads n copies of a small kernel code object; free memory counts each
+    as at least 2 MB."""
+    import triton
+    import triton.language as tl
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def add_one(x_ptr, n, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        i = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        tl.store(x_ptr + i, tl.load(x_ptr + i, mask=i < n) + 1, mask=i < n)
+
+    x = torch.zeros(128, device=DEVICE)
+    image = add_one.warmup(x, 128, BLOCK=128, grid=(1,)).asm["hsaco"]
+    with open("/proc/self/maps") as f:
+        path = next(line.split()[-1] for line in f if "libamdhip64" in line)
+    hip = ctypes.CDLL(path)
+    buffer = ctypes.create_string_buffer(image, len(image))
+    modules: list[ctypes.c_void_p] = []
+
+    def load(n: int) -> None:
+        for _ in range(n):
+            module = ctypes.c_void_p()
+            assert hip.hipModuleLoadData(ctypes.byref(module), buffer) == 0
+            modules.append(module)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+    yield load
+    for module in modules:
+        hip.hipModuleUnload(module)
+
+
+def test_code_objects_are_added_back(exact_count, code_objects):
+    """200 code objects of a few KB, each counted as at least 2 MB, are added
+    back; another process taking 1 GB meanwhile is not."""

+    assert added_alone > 200 * MB

+                "import sys, torch\n"

+                "torch.accelerator.synchronize()\n"
+                "print('ready', flush=True)\n"
+                "sys.stdin.read()\n"

+        stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,

+"""Free device memory corrected by amdgpu's exact VRAM count.
+
+hipMemGetInfo counts each allocation as at least 2 MB, so small allocations

+import os

+import torch

+from vllm.logger import init_logger

+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+KFD_TOPOLOGY_NODES = "/sys/class/kfd/kfd/topology/nodes"
+DRM_SYSFS = "/sys/class/drm"
+# sysfs VRAM total may exceed hipMemGetInfo's total by at most this share.
+VRAM_TOTAL_TOLERANCE = 0.01
+
+
+def _kfd_gpu_nodes(nodes_dir: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
+    """Properties of the KFD GPU nodes; CPU and malformed nodes are skipped."""
+    nodes = []
+    for node in sorted(os.listdir(nodes_dir)):
+        try:
+            # One "name value" pair per line.
+            with open(os.path.join(nodes_dir, node, "properties")) as f:
+                props = dict(line.split() for line in f if line.strip())
+            if int(props.get("simd_count", 0)) > 0 and "drm_render_minor" in props:
+                int(props["location_id"])
+                int(props.get("unique_id", -1))
+                nodes.append(props)
+        except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError):
+            continue
+    return nodes
+
+
+def _pci(props: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    # location_id is (bus << 8) | (dev << 3) | fn; torch reports no function.
+    loc = int(props["location_id"])
+    return int(props.get("domain", 0)), loc >> 8, (loc >> 3) & 0x1F
+
+
+def _unique_id(uuid: str) -> int | None:
+    # torch's ROCm UUID is the KFD unique_id written as ASCII hex digits.
+    try:
+        return int(bytes.fromhex(uuid.replace("-", "")).decode(), 16)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def find_vram_used_file(
+    uuid: str,
+    pci: tuple[int, int, int],
+    total_memory: int,
+    *,
+    nodes_dir: str = KFD_TOPOLOGY_NODES,
+    drm_dir: str = DRM_SYSFS,
+) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
+    """The mem_info_vram_used file of the GPU with this torch UUID and PCI
+    address, and hipMemGetInfo's total_memory; or None and why not."""
+    try:
+        nodes = _kfd_gpu_nodes(nodes_dir)
+    except OSError as e:
+        return None, f"no KFD topology ({e})"
+    unique_id = _unique_id(uuid)
+    by_uid = [n for n in nodes if int(n.get("unique_id", -1)) == unique_id]
+    by_pci = [n for n in nodes if _pci(n) == pci]
+    if len(by_pci) > 1:
+        # Partitions share one device's VRAM counter.
+        return None, "partitioned GPU"
+    if len(by_pci) != 1 or (unique_id is not None and by_uid != by_pci):
+        return None, "no single KFD node matches the GPU"
+    device_dir = os.path.join(
+        drm_dir, f"renderD{by_pci[0]['drm_render_minor']}", "device"
+    )
+    try:
+        with open(os.path.join(device_dir, "mem_info_vram_total")) as f:
+            vram_total = int(f.read())
+        with open(os.path.join(device_dir, "mem_info_vram_used")) as f:
+            int(f.read())
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
+        return None, f"no amdgpu VRAM counters ({e})"
+    # A total far from HIP's means memory HIP sees is not this VRAM (e.g. an
+    # APU's shared memory). Below HIP's would let the cap exceed real VRAM.
+    if not total_memory <= vram_total <= total_memory * (1 + VRAM_TOTAL_TOLERANCE):
+        return None, (
+            f"VRAM total {vram_total} bytes does not match HIP's {total_memory}"
+        )
+    return os.path.join(device_dir, "mem_info_vram_used"), ""
+
+
+# A reading is settled once the memory hidden from free memory has not risen
+# for this long. Freed memory stays in the exact count until the driver has
+# erased it (about 10 ms per GB on an R9700) while free memory shows it free at
+# once, which lowers what appears hidden.
+SETTLE_SECONDS = 0.2
+MAX_SAMPLING_SECONDS = 2.0
+SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 0.002
+
+# mem_info_vram_used per device index, or None where there is none.
+_vram_used_files: dict[int, str | None] = {}
+
+
+def _vram_used_file(index: int) -> str | None:
+    """Only unpartitioned discrete GPUs whose VRAM total matches HIP's."""
+    if index not in _vram_used_files:
+        props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(index)
+        if props.is_integrated:
+            path, reason = None, "integrated GPU"
+        else:
+            path, reason = find_vram_used_file(
+                str(props.uuid),
+                (props.pci_domain_id, props.pci_bus_id, props.pci_device_id),
+                torch.cuda.mem_get_info(index)[1],
+            )
+        if path is None:
+            logger.debug(
+                "Using free device memory as HIP reports it, which counts each "
+                "allocation as at least 2 MB: %s.",
+                reason,
+            )
+        _vram_used_files[index] = path
+    return _vram_used_files[index]
+
+
+def _read_used(path: str) -> int | None:
+    try:
+        with open(path) as f:
+            return int(f.read())
+    except (OSError, ValueError):
+        return None
+
+
+def exact_free_memory(device: torch.device | None = None) -> int | None:
+    """Free bytes by the exact VRAM count, or None where there is none.
+
+    At least free memory as HIP reports it, plus what that hides: the total less
+    the exact count less HIP's free memory, sampled until it stops rising. An
+    erase still pending afterwards only makes the result smaller. Other
+    processes' allocations lower both counts alike. The exact count leaves out
+    KFD's page-table reserve and RAS pages (about 80 MB on an R9700), which
+    KV_CACHE_MARGIN_FLOOR_BYTES covers.
+    """
+    index = (
+        torch.cuda.current_device()
+        if device is None or device.index is None
+        else device.index
+    )
+    path = _vram_used_file(index)
+    if path is None:
+        return None
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(index)
+    start = last_rise = time.monotonic()
+    hidden = 0
+    while True:
+        used = _read_used(path)
+        free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info(index)
+        used_after = _read_used(path)
+        if used is None or used_after is None:
+            return None
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        # Skip a sample when another process allocated between the two
+        # counts: free memory would already show it and too much seem hidden.
+        if used_after <= used and total - used - free > hidden:
+            hidden, last_rise = total - used - free, now
+        if now - last_rise >= SETTLE_SECONDS or now - start >= MAX_SAMPLING_SECONDS:
+            break
+        time.sleep(SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
+    if hidden > 0:
+        logger.info(
+            "Free device memory: %.2f GiB reported, %.2f GiB more by the exact "
+            "VRAM count.",
+            free / (1 << 30),
+            hidden / (1 << 30),
+        )
+    return free + hidden

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Lint and fix docstring style that matters once docstrings render as Markdown.
+
+- Code spans use single backticks: ``x`` is rewritten to `x` in place.
+- Python Sphinx roles become code spans of the text Sphinx would display, e.g.
+  :class:`~vllm.LLM` is rewritten to `LLM`. Other roles must be fixed by hand.
+- Sections are Google style (`Args:`), not NumPy style (`Parameters` + `---`).
+- Admonitions, code blocks and links are Markdown (`!!! note`, fences,
+  `[text](url)`), not reStructuredText (`.. note::`, `.. code-block::`,
+  `` `text <url>`_ ``).
+- Code spans do not start with a space or start or end at a line break, which
+  is how a span broken across lines or missing its closing backtick shows up.
+- Docstrings with escapes or line continuations cannot be fixed in place, so
+  any of the above in them is reported; a raw string fixes that.
+- `[a][b]` is a reference link that mkdocs-autorefs tries to resolve, so shapes
+  and indexing written outside code spans produce broken cross-references:
+
+      [block][2][16]        # BUG: looks up targets "2" and "16"
+      `[block][2][16]`      # OK: code span
+      [LLM][vllm.LLM]       # OK: intended cross-reference
+      [int][]               # OK: stdlib cross-reference
+
+All rules read docstrings as source text, one Markdown paragraph at a time, and
+skip code blocks, so reported line numbers point at the offending line.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import codecs
+import io
+import sys
+import tokenize
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import regex as re
+
+FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(`{3,}|~{3,})")
+DOCTEST = re.compile(r"^\s*>>>")
+SECTION = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z][A-Za-z ]*):\s*$")
+ADMONITION = re.compile(r"^\s*(!!!|\?\?\?\+?)\s")
+BACKTICKS = re.compile(r"`+")
+REF_LINK = re.compile(
+    r"(?<!\\)\[((?:[^\[\]]|\[[^\[\]]*\])+)\](?: |\n[ \t]*)?\[([^\[\]]*)\]"
+)
+REF_DEF = re.compile(r"^\s*\[([^\]]+)\]:\s", re.MULTILINE)
+# A Sphinx role directly before a code span, e.g. :class: or :py:meth:
+ROLE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w:`]):((?:[a-z]+:)?[a-z]+):$")
+# Explicit title, e.g. :meth:`generate <vllm.LLM.generate>`
+TITLED_ROLE = re.compile(r"\s*(.*?)\s*<[^<>]+>\s*", re.DOTALL)
+PY_ROLES = {
+    f"{domain}{role}"
+    for domain in ("", "py:")
+    for role in ("attr", "class", "const", "data", "exc", "func", "meth", "mod",
+                 "obj", "type")
+}  # fmt: skip
+NUMPY_SECTION = re.compile(
+    r"^[ \t]*(Parameters|Other Parameters|Returns|Yields|Receives|Raises|Warns|"
+    r"Attributes|Notes)[ \t]*\n[ \t]*-{3,}[ \t]*$",
+    re.MULTILINE,
+)
+RST_DIRECTIVE = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*\.\. ([a-z][a-z-]*)::", re.MULTILINE)
+RST_LINK = re.compile(r"`([^`<>]+?) ?<https?://[^<>`]+>`__?")
+# What `fix_code_spans` would rewrite, for docstrings it cannot edit
+RST_MARKUP = re.compile(r"``[^`]|:(?:[a-z]+:)?[a-z]+:`")
+QUOTE = re.compile(r"""^[rRuU]?("{3}|'{3}|"|')""")
+# Fully qualified Python paths, e.g. `vllm.LLM` or `torch.Tensor`
+TARGET = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*(\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)+")
+# Collapsed `[label][]` may also name a builtin, e.g. `[int][]`
+COLLAPSED_TARGET = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*(\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)*")
+
+# Google-style sections griffe parses; item sections nest one level deeper
+ITEM_SECTIONS = {
+    "args", "arguments", "params", "parameters", "keyword args",
+    "keyword arguments", "other args", "other arguments", "other params",
+    "other parameters", "raises", "exceptions", "warns", "receives",
+    "attributes", "functions", "methods", "classes", "modules",
+}  # fmt: skip
+SECTIONS = ITEM_SECTIONS | {
+    "returns", "yields", "examples", "example", "note", "notes", "warning",
+    "warnings", "todo", "see also", "references",
+}  # fmt: skip
+
+DEFS = (ast.ClassDef, ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
+BLOCKS = (ast.If, ast.Try, ast.With, ast.AsyncWith)
+
+
+def prose_mask(lines: list[str]) -> list[bool]:
+    """Whether each docstring line is Markdown prose (not code or blank)."""
+    lines = [line.expandtabs() for line in lines]
+    indent = min(
+        (len(line) - len(line.lstrip()) for line in lines[1:] if line.strip()),
+        default=0,
+    )
+    mask: list[bool] = []
+    fence = None
+    container: tuple[int, int] | None = None  # (header indent, code indent)
+    code = doctest = False
+    prev_blank = True
+    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+        text = QUOTE.sub("", line) if i == 0 else line[indent:]
+        stripped = text.strip()
+        if fence:
+            mask.append(False)
+            if len(stripped) >= len(fence) and set(stripped) == {fence[0]}:
+                fence = None
+            continue
+        if not stripped:
+            mask.append(False)
+            doctest, prev_blank = False, True
+            continue
+        ind = len(text) - len(text.lstrip())
+        if container and ind <= container[0]:
+            container = None
+        code = ind >= (container[1] if container else 4) and (prev_blank or code)
+        prev_blank = False
+        if not code and (match := FENCE.match(text)):
+            fence = match.group(1)
+            mask.append(False)
+            continue
+        doctest = not code and (doctest or bool(DOCTEST.match(text)))
+        prose = not (code or doctest)
+        mask.append(prose)
+        section = SECTION.match(text) if prose else None
+        if section and (title := section.group(1).lower()) in SECTIONS:
+            container = (ind, ind + (12 if title in ITEM_SECTIONS else 8))
+        elif prose and ADMONITION.match(text):
+            container = (ind, ind + 8)
+    return mask
+
+
+def paragraphs(lines: list[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[int, int]]:
+    """Line ranges of the prose paragraphs in a docstring."""
+    start = None
+    for i, prose in enumerate([*prose_mask(lines), False]):
+        if prose and start is None:
+            start = i
+        elif not prose and start is not None:
+            yield start, i
+            start = None
+
+
+def code_spans(text: str) -> Iterator[tuple[int, int, int]]:
+    """(start, end, backtick count) of each Markdown code span in a paragraph."""
+    runs = [m.span() for m in BACKTICKS.finditer(text)]
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(runs):
+        start, end = runs[i]
+        width = end - start
+        close = next(
+            (j for j in range(i + 1, len(runs)) if runs[j][1] - runs[j][0] == width),
+            None,
+        )
+        if (start and text[start - 1] == "\\") or close is None:
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        yield start, runs[close][1], width
+        i = close + 1
+
+
+def docstrings(tree: ast.Module, rendered_only: bool) -> list[ast.Constant]:
+    """Docstring constants; `rendered_only` keeps what mkdocstrings shows.
+
+    That is module, class, function and attribute docstrings (including
+    `self.x` in `__init__`), under `if`/`try`/`with` blocks too, but not other
+    docstrings inside function bodies.
+    """
+    found: dict[int, ast.Constant] = {}
+
+    def is_str(node: ast.AST) -> bool:
+        return isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str)
+
+    def visit(node: ast.AST) -> None:
+        body = getattr(node, "body", [])
+        if body and isinstance(body[0], ast.Expr) and is_str(body[0].value):
+            found[id(body[0].value)] = body[0].value
+        if isinstance(node, (ast.Module, ast.ClassDef)) or (
+            isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "__init__"
+        ):

+    def scope(body: list[ast.stmt]) -> None:
+        prev = None
+        for stmt in body:
+            if (
+                isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr)
+                and is_str(stmt.value)
+                and isinstance(prev, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign))
+            ):
+                found[id(stmt.value)] = stmt.value
+            if isinstance(stmt, DEFS):
+                visit(stmt)
+            elif isinstance(stmt, BLOCKS):
+                scope(stmt.body)
+                scope(getattr(stmt, "orelse", []))
+                scope(getattr(stmt, "finalbody", []))
+                for handler in getattr(stmt, "handlers", []):
+                    scope(handler.body)
+            prev = stmt
+
+    visit(tree)
+    if not rendered_only:
+        for node in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(node, DEFS):
+                visit(node)

+
+
+def segment(lines: list[str], node: ast.Constant) -> tuple[str, list[str], str] | None:
+    """Split a docstring's source lines into (head, string lines, tail).

+    first, last = node.lineno - 1, node.end_lineno - 1
+    body = lines[first : last + 1]
+    # AST column offsets count UTF-8 bytes

   }'
 ```
 
+#### Extensible KV cache
+
+The extensible KV cache (`--enable-extensible-kv-cache`) maps the KV cache with the driver's virtual memory API. Within a host, UCX can only reach that memory over NVLink through a CUDA fabric handle, which takes an IMEX channel; without one it falls back to TCP. So with NIXL on device memory and no channel, vLLM leaves the extensible KV cache off.
+
+To use both within a host, make a channel available to every prefill and decode process, for example:
+
+```bash
+major=$(awk '$2 == "nvidia-caps-imex-channels" {print $1}' /proc/devices)
+mkdir -p /dev/nvidia-caps-imex-channels
+mknod /dev/nvidia-caps-imex-channels/channel0 c "$major" 0
+```
+
+Check the transport with `UCX_PROTO_INFO=y`: KV reads should show `cuda_ipc`, not `tcp`. Transfers across hosts use RDMA and need no channel: pass `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` to keep the feature on.
+
